citations: Fortera has signed a multi-year agreement with Meta covering environmental attribute certificates (EACs) associated with approximately 200,000 tons of its low-carbon cement, in a deal designed to help finance production expansion.
Meta will also have the option to use the cement in its own construction projects and expand the agreement’s volume or duration in future years.
The agreement provides a long-term demand signal for lower-emission construction materials, potentially giving Fortera greater revenue certainty as it seeks funding for new facilities.
The partnership is expected to support development of Fortera’s planned cement plant in Ste. Genevieve, Missouri.

The facility is designed to produce ReAct Cement, which uses captured carbon dioxide (CO2) and, according to Fortera, generates 70% fewer emissions than ordinary Portland cement production. The product has undergone third-party testing and meets ASTM standards for use in concrete.
The plant is planned to produce 300,000 tons of cement annually. Fortera already operates a facility in Redding, California, with annual capacity of 15,000 tons.
notes: All claims are supported by the Carbon Herald article: multi-year Meta EAC agreement for ~200,000 tons of low-carbon cement; option for Meta to use cement and expand volume/duration; long-term revenue visibility and financing support; planned Ste. Genevieve, Missouri plant producing 300,000 tons/yr of ReAct Cement; 70% fewer emissions than ordinary Portland cement per Fortera; third-party testing and ASTM standards.

Capacity status is correctly framed: Ste. Genevieve is described as 'planned' (300,000 t/yr), and the Redding, California facility (15,000 t/yr) is described as already operating; the candidate does not misstate the Missouri plant as operational.

The candidate correctly flags that signing date, duration, price, EAC methodology, CO2 source, chemistry, energy use, FID, timeline, capex, LCA boundary and independent verification are not provided in the source.
Authority check passes: the candidate is marked secondary and Carbon Herald is a named trade publication reporting the development.
No legal/regulatory claims are made, so legal_status_effective_date is inapplicable and passes.
Only English claims are present; translation_meaning is inapplicable and passes.

citations: Montreal, November 2, 2026 – CarbiCrete, a leading firm in the decarbonization of concrete, has supplied Amazon with three different products at a new Amazon UK delivery station in Stockton-on-Tees.
In the first wide-scale deployment of its cement-free pavers anywhere in the world, CarbiCrete products now cover around 6,400m² of paving across parking spaces and footpaths at the site.
The delivery station is Amazon’s first building to pursue the latest version (v1.1) of Living Future’s Zero Carbon Certification

CarbiCrete’s technology replaces 100% of the cement content in masonry and hardscape products with a steel-making by-product, avoiding cement-related emissions. The company then uses carbon dioxide to cure its concrete, permanently storing captured carbon within the products
“Seeing CarbiCrete products deployed at this scale is an important milestone for our technology and for lower-carbon construction more broadly.,” says Gary Belisle, CarbiCrete’s CEO.
notes: All claims are supported by the source text: three products supplied to Amazon's new Stockton-on-Tees UK delivery station; ~6,400 m² of paving across parking spaces and footpaths; described as first wide-scale deployment of cement-free pavers anywhere; binder replaces 100% of cement in masonry and hardscape with a steel-making by-product; CO2 curing permanently stores captured carbon; building is Amazon's first to pursue Living Future Zero Carbon Certification v1.1.
